result.question: How does Nvidia describe competition for its data center products?
result.answer:
Nvidia describes its target markets, including data center products, as remaining competitive, with competition that may intensify due to expanding and changing product and service offerings, industry standards, customer and market needs, new entrants, and consolidations [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. The company states that competitors compete on a wide range of parameters including price, total cost of ownership, and performance, which has resulted and may in the future result in lower-than-expected selling prices or demand for its products [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. Some competitors operate their own fabrication facilities and have longer operating histories, larger customer bases, more comprehensive IP portfolios and patent protections, more design wins, and greater financial, sales, marketing, and distribution resources than Nvidia [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. These competitors may acquire market share, more effectively identify and capitalize on new market opportunities, transition products more quickly, and impinge on Nvidia's ability to procure sufficient foundry capacity and scarce input materials during supply-constrained environments [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001].

Specific to data center products, Nvidia notes that some of its customers are developing their own ASICs and other products, including designs optimized for certain workloads that may not require all of the features and functionality Nvidia's data center systems provide [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. Others may offer cloud-based services that compete with Nvidia's AI cloud service offerings, and Nvidia may not be able to establish market share sufficient to achieve the scale necessary to meet its business objectives [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. Additionally, Nvidia's competitive position has been harmed by export controls, and its competitive position and future results will be further harmed over the long term if restrictions remain in place or are expanded, if customers purchase products from competitors, or if customers develop their own internal solutions [0001045810-26-000021:item-1-p017]. The Chinese government has encouraged customers to purchase from Nvidia's China-based competitors and discouraged customers from purchasing, importing, or using Nvidia's data center products [0001045810-26-000021:item-1-p017]. If Nvidia is unable to successfully compete in this environment, demand for its products, services, and technologies could decrease, which may negatively impact its business [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001].
